reviews.title: Great App - but let me track salt!
reviews.text:
Update: I have decided to remove a star from my review, as the app still won't let me track salt, and two months and two emails later, Customer Care refuse to help me, despite telling me to email them. 

Update: I had already emailed customer care on the 10th August, before the developer response, and have not had a response since. My app is definitely not set for the US. So my review remains unchanged at this time.

I love this app, but I'm getting frustrated as I want to be able to track salt and NOT sodium - and the app description says I can track salt. But I can't switch it from sodium! Even my mums android app lets her track salt. And I can't find any info online about why only my app and account seems to be stuck on sodium instead of salt.

reviews.title: Subscription blocking
reviews.text:
Was very impressed with the app until my free trial ran out. I chose not to subscribe as it’s not within my budget to pay out for it. 
I didn’t expect to have a limit on how many food items I can add per day (5 items) without the subscription in place. This has really disappointed me as I was starting my health journey to loose weight by calorie counting which this app was brilliant for and now I can’t even add everything I had for breakfast and lunch. 

Overall the app is brilliant if you have the money for the subscription, however isn’t worth the time of day without it.

reviews.title: Dangerous defaults
reviews.text: Tried this app after being guided from NHS weight loss app to My Fitness Pal by a nutritionist. MFP’s terrible database of inaccurately entered product data exhausted me but my staples are all there now. I was looking for a British centric alternative and found NutraCheck. My issue is that I have piled on weight during traumatic injuries and I need to maintain protein intake for rehabilitation whilst cutting back calories during training. NutraCheck would not allow me to enter my target weight after 30 weeks as it considered it too aggressive but then it gave me a 1200 calorie limit which is a starvation diet totally inappropriate for anyone who needs to maintain strength and stamina. I was losing 1kg/week on NHS Weight Loss at 1400 calories per day and reduced this loss to 0.6kg/week on MFP at 1800 calories per day. NutraCheck would have made me lose weight at double my target rate and could have wrecked my rehabilitation. Fortunately past experience saved me from this blunder.
